newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 28.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- President Kim Young-sam will make a statment to the nation on May 30 concerning his 1992 presidential campaign funding.
- Opposition leaders, Kim Dae-jung and Kim Jong-pil, demanded that President Kim Young-sam appear at the National Assembly and apologise over the 1992 campaign financing.

- Major industrial countries agreed on Tuesday to outlaw corporate bribery of officials in international deals, conclude a multilateral accord on cross-border investment and push for regulatory reform.

- About 200,000 political prisoners are scattered in about 10 concentration camps in the North, and Pyongyang exercises tight control over the prisoners by constantly moving these camps, said a human rights report.
- South Korean Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik reiterated Seoul's position that Korea will treat both domestic and foreign goods equally.
